transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-08-27
- Time: 4:00 PM PDT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Zhou (Redwood SE), Aditi Menon (Redwood CSM); Maya Ortiz, Ben Cho, Priya Rao, Omar Singh (NimbleRetail)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, possibly noisy):
Redwood and NimbleRetail walked through last week's benchmark batch. Primary focus on TTFT variance during microbursts and streaming handshake jitter. Discussed sequence length heuristics to force kernel switch earlier for long prompts; agreed to run microburst with KV prefetch and alternate kernel path.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda, well run through the numbers from fridays run, then lena will talk kernel variants, then action items. Maya you good?
[00:08] Maya: yeah thx, sorry i was on another standup so, um, thanks. were keen to get ttft down for our chat flows, early tokens are... expensive for us, customers notice lag.
[00:18] Lena: cool, so from our side we re-ran the streambench with the three kernel profiles: baseline fastpath, quantized fallback and the new streaming-hedge path. baseline median TTFT was 42ms, 95th 87ms; hedge path brought median to 36ms but 95th stayed around 95ms because of microburst tailing.
[00:39] Ben: quick q, when you say hedge path, is that the one that does early-kv prefetch? we saw sometimes kv cache miss causes a spike.
[00:45] Lena: yeah hedge does speculative KV prefetch and a shorter kernel for first tokens, it also autoswitches at seqlen 96 in this run. but we think the autoswitch point might need tuning per workload.
[00:58] Maya: our average seqlen's more like 30 in interactive, but occasional system prompts push to 220. that's the problem, right? long tails.
[01:06] Samir: exactly. and theres also the streaming handshake overhead, which is like a 6-12ms per-request tax depending on network. across bursts it stacks.
[01:15] Omar: can you remind us of the difference between hosted route and dedicated route here? were sensitive to cost but latency matters for checkout flow.
[01:24] Samir: hosted is our standard infra route, multi-tenant with good perf for steady QPS. dedicated is reserved GPU pools with lower jitter; for microbursts dedicated plus kernel hedging tends to win but cost is higher. we can also do hybrid routing: primary hosted, canary to dedicated for high-priority traffic.
[01:39] Priya: and VPC? if we go private, does the RTT change much? were worried about vpc egress and private networking.
[01:45] Lena: VPC adds network hops but gives you control of routing; we've seen roughly +5-15ms depending on region and peering. however, it lowers cross-tenant noisy neighbor jitter.
[01:58] Ben: the sheet shows a weird spike at run 427, any idea?
[02:02] Lena: that was when the kernel swapped mid-response because seqlen sniff hit 128, the kv cache had a miss and we fell back to quant path, so you get a compound penalty.
[02:13] Maya: could we just cap seqlen and truncate system prompts to reduce kernel switches?
[02:18] Samir: yes that's one strategy; another is to use heuristic routing: if predicted length > 120 route to dedicated fast kernels. but that needs accurate prediction and tagging in upstream.
[02:29] Omar: tagging seems doable, we can add header. but wed prefer platform-side heuristics if possible.
[02:34] Samir: we can do a model of incoming tokens and route in the gateway; that's what the hybrid routing prototype does.
[02:40] Ben: what about streaming handshake jitter -- is that mitigable?
[02:43] Lena: partly. we shortened the RTT by collapsing chunk sizes and moving to websocket keepalive; that shaved 8-10ms. the rest comes from kernel warmup on cold sequences and cache misses.
[02:53] Maya: your microburst tests last week were with 1000 reqs, right? wed like to see 10k to simulate peak holiday load.
[02:59] Lena: correct, last run was 1k. well schedule 10k with three kernel variants and KV prefetch this weekend. we expect results early monday.
[03:10] Priya: please include the slow path traces; those are the most helpful for our SRE team.
[03:14] Lena: yes will include full traces and per-token timing CSV.
[03:18] Samir: on the cost front, quick math: dedicated reserved will be about 2-3x host cost but reduces tail latency; good for checkout traffic. well send an updated pricing/commit sheet.
[03:28] Maya: also, security question: we need SOC2 type II and KMS integration for keys in the private deploy. is that ready?
[03:34] Aditi: yes we have SOC2, and KMS/HSM integrations are supported in private deployments. will share the compliance pack link after this.
[03:41] Omar: do you support customer-managed HSM for on-prem?
[03:44] Samir: yes, optional package for private deployments. we can do a short POC on a dev HSM if you want.
[03:49] Ben: one more: do kernel choices affect tokenization differences? we saw slight output variance across quantized fallback.
[03:56] Lena: small differences can appear with aggressive quant, which is why we recommend running eval prompts — we do regression checks when switching quant profiles to make sure quality delta is acceptable.
[04:05] Maya: ok, lets talk concrete experiments: 1) 10k microburst with KV prefetch/hedge, 2) a run with seqlen cap 128 and upstream tag routing, 3) dedicated canary for checkout path at 5% traffic.
[04:17] Samir: agreed. well also include a run that simulates VPC peering to capture the extra RTT.
[04:22] Priya: will you also capture first byte and first token separately? we need TTFT and TTF token split.
[04:27] Lena: yes per-token timing exported, first byte and first token split included.
[04:31] Omar: timeline?
[04:33] Samir: bench by 8/31, Nimble to share SLOs by 9/1, kernel deep-dive 9/3. well sync after bench to choose route.
[04:40] Maya: sounds good. thanks all.
[04:42] Samir: any blockers?
[04:44] Ben: none on infra, just need the CSV and traces.
[04:46] Priya: same.
[04:47] Samir: awesome, well wrap. ill drop notes and links in the sheet.
[04:52] Aditi: sharing links now, please ping if anything missing.
